clue.text: International group fades away — it's pants!

parts.note: the UN, the United Nations, is a group of nations
to fade away is to die out, so dies

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a feeble international organisation as rubbish, using the slang 'pants'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's pants!' reads as British slang for 'it's rubbish', but 'pants' is the definition in its other British sense: underpants.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain pants are underpants, and undies is a casual word for underwear.

clue.text: Standard, without elite service?

parts.note: without means having no, so no
RM, the Royal Marines, is an elite branch of the armed services

explanation.surface: A question about whether ordinary service is all you get when the elite option is missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elite service' reads as top-class customer service, but it is the Royal Marines, abbreviated RM.
explanation.definitionFit: A norm is the accepted standard or usual level against which things are judged.

clue.text: Hatched at home, baby animal, a bear!

parts.note: someone at home is said to be in
a cub is the young of a bear, lion or fox
Ted, as in teddy, stands for a toy bear

explanation.surface: An excited announcement that a baby bear has hatched at home.
explanation.walkthrough: TED, short for teddy, is the crossword's usual bear.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggs that are incubated are kept warm until they hatch, and a plan incubated is one hatched over time.

clue.text: Lecture Carol briefly, concealing sound of hesitation

indicators.note: concealing means the shortened song word holds the hesitation sound inside it
briefly asks for the word for carol to be cut short by its final letter

parts.note: a carol is a Christmas song
erm is the noise a speaker makes while hesitating

explanation.surface: Someone telling off a person called Carol, who hides her hesitation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carol' looks like a woman's name but is a Christmas song; 'briefly' trims SONG to SON, and 'concealing' puts ERM inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sermon is a moral talk delivered from the pulpit, so a lecture in both senses.

clue.text: Woolly stuff shrank in the end — wet with rain unfortunately

indicators.note: in the end points to the final letter of the word shrank
unfortunately signals that the letters of wet and rain come out in an unlucky jumble

explanation.surface: A woollen jumper ended up shrinking after it got soaked in the rain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the end' gives K from shrank; 'unfortunately' rearranges WET and RAIN into NITWEAR; 'with' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Knitted garments such as jumpers and cardigans are typically made of wool.

clue.text: Calm down there puny oiks or … putting it another way …

indicators.note: putting it another way says the preceding words are to be rearranged into a different form

explanation.surface: Someone telling off a gang of weedy louts, then trailing off to rephrase the warning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting it another way' rearranges THERE PUNY OIKS OR into the phrase. An oik is British slang for an uncouth person; the idiom fits the clothing theme running through the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom tells an angry person to stay calm rather than start a fight.

clue.text: Carve lines within boundaries surrounding stash at head rapper's house

indicators.note: surrounding means those inner letters go round the rest of the pieces
within boundaries means only the part of lines inside its first and last letters
at head takes the opening letter of stash

parts.note: crib is hip-hop slang for one's home, as in the TV show MTV Cribs

explanation.surface: Instructions to carve lines round a hidden stash at the front of a rapper's mansion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'within boundaries' gives INE, the inside of 'lines'; 'surrounding' wraps it round S (from 'at head' of stash) plus CRIB, giving IN-SCRIB-E.
explanation.definitionFit: To inscribe is to cut or engrave words into a surface such as stone.

clue.text: With assistance dog, just a pup!

parts.note: assistance is help

explanation.surface: Someone notes that their assistance dog is still only a puppy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assistance dog' reads as one phrase, a guide dog, but 'assistance' is HELP and 'dog' only joins it to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A whelp is a young dog that has not yet grown up.

clue.text: Those I'm sending to plug outfits being worn by Earl

parts.note: a plug is a piece of publicity, an ad

indicators.note: being worn by means the outfits word goes round the earl's letter, as clothes go round a body

parts.note: dresses are outfits

explanation.surface: Someone advertising outfits modelled by an aristocrat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plug' is a promotional mention, AD; 'being worn by' puts DRESSES round E, making DRESSE-E-S.
explanation.definitionFit: The people a letter is sent to are its recipients, those named on the envelope.

clue.text: Sparrow's head maybe covered with this twinkling gold crown of narrow lines

definitions.text: Sparrow's head maybe covered with this

indicators.note: lines means the gold and narrow pieces form a lining inside the twinkling word

parts.note: in a twinkling means in a trice, an instant
or is the heraldic word for gold

indicators.note: crown of takes the top, first letter of narrow

explanation.surface: A glittering golden hat with fine lines, fit for a sparrow's head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sparrow' is the pirate Captain Jack Sparrow, who wears a three-cornered hat, not the bird. 'lines' puts OR + N inside TRICE.
explanation.definitionFit: This three-cornered hat was worn by eighteenth-century sailors and pirates, such as the film character.

clue.text: Sports brand known for illegally importing small parrots?!

definitions.text: Sports brand known for illegally importing small parrots?!

parts.words: Sports brand known for illegally importing small parrots?!
parts.note: the swimwear brand's tight trunks are called budgie smugglers in Australian slang, so it smuggles small parrots

explanation.surface: A sportswear company accused of smuggling budgerigars.
explanation.walkthrough: Tight men's swimming trunks are known in Australia as 'budgie smugglers'; budgies are small parrots, and this brand is the one most associated with them.
explanation.definitionFit: The Australian swimwear brand makes the close-fitting trunks nicknamed after smuggled budgerigars.

clue.text: Hid dangerous devices in bra?

parts.note: read one way, concealed explosives were planted; read another, breasts are held in a bra

explanation.surface: A smuggler accused of hiding weapons in underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer means rigged with hidden explosives; the question mark invites a second reading with 'booby' as slang for a breast, held captive in a bra.
explanation.definitionFit: A place fitted with concealed explosives set to go off when touched is rigged in this way.

clue.text: Then gull flew, half-hidden, manoeuvring down to the ground

indicators.note: manoeuvring tells us the letters are moved around into new positions
half-hidden means only the first half of flew stays visible

explanation.surface: A seagull takes off and wheels about before coming back to land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-hidden' keeps FL, the visible half of 'flew'; 'manoeuvring' rearranges THEN + GULL + FL.
explanation.definitionFit: A full-length garment reaches all the way down to the floor.

clue.text: Fit clubs?

explanation.definitionFit: To suit is to fit or become someone; clubs is one of the four card groups, along with hearts, diamonds and spades.

clue.text: Reduce rurality of milling barn I use

indicators.note: milling suggests grinding things up, so the words barn I use are churned into a new order

explanation.surface: A farmer explains how they convert a barn for milling grain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'milling' looks like the farm work done in the barn, but it rearranges BARN I USE.
explanation.definitionFit: To urbanise an area is to make it more like a town and less like countryside.

clue.text: Clothing for rest of nearby settlement stopped by government

parts.note: nigh means near

indicators.note: stopped by means the settlement word is plugged by the government letter in its middle

parts.note: a town is a settlement

explanation.surface: Clothes for the people of a nearby village, whose rest is interrupted by officials.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stopped by' puts G inside TOWN to make TGOWN, after NIGH.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightgown is a loose garment worn to sleep in.

clue.text: Iniesta cycling following run, having more showers than anyone!

indicators.note: following puts the footballer's name after the run letter in the answer

parts.note: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for run

indicators.note: cycling means the letters of Iniesta wheel round, the last moving to the front

explanation.surface: The Spanish footballer Andrés Iniesta goes for a bike ride after a jog and needs a lot of showers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycling' moves the final A of INIESTA to the front, giving AINIEST, which goes after R.
explanation.definitionFit: The rainiest place gets more rain showers than any other.

clue.text: Do threads run through D&G's gala supply?

indicators.note: through means the run letter passes into the middle of the mixed letters
supply here is the adverb of supple, so the letters bend into a new shape

parts.note: the letters D, G and the S of the possessive, from the fashion label Dolce & Gabbana

explanation.surface: A question about whether the Dolce & Gabbana gala uses fancy fabrics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' is a party, not a verb, and 'supply' is supple-ly, meaning flexibly: it rearranges D, G, S and GALA, with R from 'run' put inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Glad rags are one's best clothes, worn to a party or do.

clue.text: Grocers regularly disposed of leaves

indicators.note: regularly disposed of means every other letter of grocers is thrown away

explanation.surface: Greengrocers routinely throw away old lettuce leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' looks like the noun for foliage, but it is the verb: someone departs.
explanation.definitionFit: When someone goes, they depart or leave.

clue.text: Avoids parodies involving monarch

indicators.note: involving means the parodies word takes in the monarch's letter

parts.note: skits are comic parodies
R stands for rex or regina, king or queen

explanation.surface: Someone steers clear of comedy sketches that mock the king.
explanation.walkthrough: R, from Latin rex or regina, is the usual crossword monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: To skirt a problem is to go round it rather than face it.

clue.text: Pass child in chair that is clutching designer top from Tagliatore

indicators.note: in puts the child word inside the chair word

parts.note: a seat is a chair
a son is a child

indicators.note: clutching means the abbreviation for that is holds the designer's initials

parts.note: ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is
CK is Calvin Klein, the fashion designer

indicators.note: top from takes the first letter of Tagliatore

explanation.surface: A child perched in a seat holds a garment from the Italian tailoring label Tagliatore.
explanation.walkthrough: CK is Calvin Klein. SEA(SON)T, then I(CK)E, then T.
explanation.definitionFit: A season ticket is a pass allowing repeated travel or entry over a period.

clue.text: Crept stealthily, alone, carrying Tutankhamen's head

indicators.note: carrying means the word for alone holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: sole means alone, the only one

indicators.note: head means the first letter of Tutankhamen

explanation.surface: A tomb robber creeps in alone, making off with the pharaoh's head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying' puts T, the first letter of Tutankhamen, inside SOLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Stole is the past tense of steal in its sense of moving quietly and unseen.

clue.text: Inane avaricious rise of artificial intelligence creates division on Earth

indicators.note: inane can mean empty, so the word avaricious is emptied of all but its first and last letters
rise of, in a down clue, means the abbreviation is read upwards, backwards

explanation.surface: A complaint that the foolish, greedy growth of AI is splitting the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inane' looks like an insult but means empty: AVARICIOUS loses its inside, leaving AS. 'rise of' turns AI upwards to IA.
explanation.definitionFit: A continent is one of the great land divisions of the globe.

clue.text: Take no notice of contents of sign or explanation

indicators.note: contents of means the letters are found inside the run of words sign or explanation

explanation.surface: Advice to disregard what a notice or its explanation says.
explanation.definitionFit: To ignore something is to disregard it and pay it no attention.

clue.text: One who's slow to get up, admitting troublesome oversleeping primarily

indicators.note: admitting means the phrase for getting up lets the initial letters in

parts.note: to rise is to get up from bed

indicators.note: primarily takes the first letter of each of the words troublesome and oversleeping

explanation.surface: A habitual late riser who has a nasty habit of sleeping in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One who's slow to get up' looks like the definition, but only 'One who's slow' is, the reptile of the fable; 'admitting' puts TO inside TO RISE.
explanation.definitionFit: In Aesop's fable of the race with the hare, this reptile is the proverbially slow creature.

clue.text: Perhaps shake fist at Playhouse moving Republican towards the front — hint of nepotism?

indicators.note: moving says one letter of the playhouse word changes position
towards the front says the letter shifts nearer the start of the word

parts.note: a playhouse is a theatre

indicators.note: hint of means just the first letter of nepotism

explanation.surface: A theatre promotes a Republican's relative, and someone rages at the favouritism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving ... towards the front' shifts the R of THEATRE forward to give THREATE, and N is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaking a fist at someone is one example of a menacing gesture, hence 'Perhaps'.

clue.text: Upon review, trial a DNase derivative that's designed to protect foot

indicators.note: upon review means the drawn-out letters are read looking back, right to left
derivative means letters are drawn from inside the words trial a DNase

explanation.surface: A lab test of an enzyme-based product intended to treat feet.
explanation.walkthrough: DNase is an enzyme that breaks down DNA. 'derivative' draws LADNAS from 'triaL A DNASe', and 'Upon review' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: This open shoe of straps and a sole protects the foot.
